Expected.Finding: Moisture conditioning refers to allowing the print to absorb moisture. This is inevitble since nylons are hygroscopic, but you can expedite the process by keeping the print in a high humidity climate, or submerging them in water, for 48 hours. All of our test specimens were annealed at 100˚C for 16 hours, and then immerged in water at 60˚C for 48 hours. The average moisture content of specimens is 2.57%.
Expected.Exposure / conditions: Maker FAQ treatment sequence and moisture context only; compare to own TDS conditions before using it. No additional measurement or service/hydrolysis test inferred.
